### Observed differences

- Six activities became optional. Earlier, A22 and each of A31, A32, A37, A38, A39 ran in every one of the 200 traces; in the later window A22 runs in about 45 in 100 traces (91 of 200) and each of the five others in about 55 in 100 (110 of 200). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- A22 and the five-activity block became mutually exclusive. Earlier every trace contained both, with the block running before A22; in the later window they co-occur in only about 1 in 200 traces, while about 45 in 100 traces contain only A22 and about 55 in 100 only the block. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019]
- The block changed its place in the flow. Earlier, A20's outgoing transitions all led into the block (spread over the five members at roughly 17–24% each), and the block preceded both A23 and A21 in all traces. In the later window, A20 leads almost always directly to A23 (about 995 in 1000 outgoing transitions), and the block, when it runs, follows A21 and A23 and precedes A26 (block before A21 in about 1 in 200 traces, versus all traces earlier). [DIR001, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029]
- A21's routing changed accordingly. Earlier it always led to A22; in the later window about 45% of its outgoing transitions go to A22 and the rest to the block members (about 7–17% each), whose outgoing transitions now typically reach A26 (about 14–25%) rather than A23. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]
- Event positions moved consistently with this: the block's mean position shifted from about 0.40 to about 0.57–0.59 of the trace, while A23 (0.48 to 0.38) and A21 (0.62 to 0.53) moved earlier. [POS002, POS004, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010]
- Within the block, pairs of activities still appear in both orders in similar proportions, so its internal sequencing remains unfixed in both windows. [REL030, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, REL037, REL038, REL039]
- The elapsed time between consecutive completions of A26 and A19 fell from about 0.9 hours to about 0.45 hours on average (56 observations in each window). [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the block A31, A32, A37, A38, A39 was given a new place in the flow and made an alternative to A22. Earlier every case ran A20, then the block (in mixed internal order), then A23 and A21, then A22, then A26. In the later window the frame A20 → A23 → A21 → … → A26 still runs in full, but A20 leads straight to A23, and after A21 the case takes one of two branches: the block, which runs to A26 in about 55 in 100 cases, or A22 alone, which runs to A26 in about 45 in 100; block and A22 essentially never both run, whereas earlier both always did. [DIR001, DIR002, OCC001, OCC002, REL007, REL008, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL019, REL020, REL024, REL025, REL029]

The support is direct and consistent: the control-flow screening produced 72 qualifying items against roughly 0.7 expected for an unchanged process (about 100 times the chance expectation); the relational items show the order reversal (block before A21/A23 in all earlier traces, after them in about 55 in 100 later traces) and the new exclusivity outright; the successor changes at A20 and A21 match them; and the position shifts point the same way. [DIR001, DIR002, REL008, REL012, REL015, REL019, REL020, REL024, POS004, POS006, screening]

Limitations: the ten lag items each rest on a single after-window observation and add little weight; the evidence shows the split between the two branches but cannot show what determines which branch a case takes (any such driver is unobserved); and the block's internal order stays unfixed, so the hypothesis treats the five activities as one unit. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]

Other differences: the elapsed time between consecutive completions of A26 and A19 roughly halved (mean about 0.94 to 0.45 hours, 56 observations in each window); as the only time item (1 against about 0.02 expected by chance in the time family), it is within what an unchanged process occasionally produces, so it is not established as a timing change and is kept out of the structural hypothesis above. [TWAIT001, screening]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening:
- units_tested: 183, items_expected_without_change: 0.74
- by_family:
  - control_flow: 144 units tested, 72 items, 0.72 expected
  - time: 39 units tested, 1 item, 0.019 expected

So control flow: 72 items vs 0.72 expected — that's 100x the chance expectation. This is a massive count, cannot be explained by chance. Time: 1 item vs 0.019 expected — that's ~50x the expectation. Hmm, but the guidance says "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces". For time: 1 item when 0.019 expected — is 1 item "of the same order" as 0.019? 0.019 expected means roughly 1 in 50 stable processes would produce one item. Hmm. The example given: "one or two items when fewer than one is expected" — that's exactly the case here for time. So the single TWAIT item alone would be what an unchanged process occasionally produces. But the control-flow family has 72 items vs 0.72 expected — that's a count many times larger, cannot be explained by chance.

So overall, there is clearly a change in control flow. The question is what hypothesis the evidence supports.

Let me reconstruct the process behaviour.

Before window (200 traces):
- A20: participation 1.0, mean 1.0 per trace (OCC for A20 not in evidence but POS001 support 200, participation 1.0). Actually OCC items are for A22, A31, A32, A37, A38, A39. A20, A21, A23, A26 have participation 1.0 in both windows (POS support 1.0).
- A22: before participation 1.0, after 0.455 (91/200).
- A31, A32, A37, A38, A39: before participation 1.0 each, after 0.55 (110/200).

DIR001: A20's outgoing transitions. Before: A32 0.17, A37 0.175, A38 0.235, A39 0.18, A31 0.24 — spread over five successors. After: A23 0.995, A37 0.005. So in the later window, A20 is almost always followed directly by A23.

DIR002: A21's outgoing. Before: A22 1.0 (always A22). After: A22 0.455, A32 0.17, A38 0.12, A39 0.095, A31 0.07, A37 0.09. So after, A21 leads to A22 in ~45.5% of its outgoing transitions and to the group A31/A32/A37/A38/A39 in the rest.

DIR003-007: A31, A32, A37, A38, A39 outgoing. Before: each spreads to A23, A31/A32/A37/A38/A39 (i.e., the group members lead to each other and to A23). After: each leads to A26 (new component ~0.14-0.25), and A23 share drops to ~0 (except A38 keeps 0.009).

So the picture: Before, there's a loop/cluster: A20 → {A31, A32, A37, A38, A39} → {each other, A23} ... and A21 → A22 → ... Let me reconstruct more.

REL items:
- REL001 (A20, A22): before co-occur 1.0, A20 before A22 1.0. After: co-occur 0.455, A_only (A20 without A22) 0.545. So A22 became optional after A20.
- REL002-006 (A20 with A31/A32/A37/A38/A39): before co-occur 1.0, A20 before B 1.0. After: co-occur 0.55, A20-only 0.45. So those five activities became optional too.
- REL007 (A21, A22): before co-occur 1.0, A21 before A22 1.0. After: co-occur 0.455, A21-only 0.545. So A22 became optional after A21 as well.
- REL008-012 (A21 with A31/A32/A37/A38/A39): before co-occurrence 1.0 with B_before_A 1.0 (i.e., A31 before A21). After: co-occurrence 0.55, A21 before B 0.545, B before A 0.005. So the order flipped: before, the group activity came before A21; after, A21 comes before the group activity. Wait — that's a big ordering change. Before: A31 → ... → A21. After: A21 → ... → A31.

Hmm wait, let me re-read. REL008: values [A21, A31]. A = A21, B = A31. Before: A_before_B = 0.0, B_before_A = 1.0. So A31 before A21 in all traces. After: A_before_B = 0.545, B_before_A = 0.005. So A21 before A31 in ~55 in 100 traces.

- REL013 (A22, A23): before co-occur 1.0, B_before_A 1.0 (A23 before A22). After: co-occur 0.455, B_only (A23 without A22) 0.545, B_before_A 0.455. So A23 always occurs; A22 became optional.
- REL014 (A22, A26): before co-occur 1.0, A22 before A26 1.0. After: co-occur 0.455, A26-only 0.545, A22 before A26 0.455. So A26 always occurs; A22 optional before it.
- REL015-019 (A22 with A31/A32/A37/A38/A39): before co-occur 1.0, B_before_A 1.0 (group before A22). After: co-occurrence 0.005 (essentially never together!), A_only (A22 without group) 0.45, B_only (group without A22) 0.545. So A22 and the group became mutually exclusive alternatives! Before they always co-occurred (group first, then A22); after, in ~45% of traces only A22, in ~55% only the group, and almost never both.

- REL020-024 (A23 with A31/A32/A37/A38/A39): before co-occur 1.0, B_before_A 1.0 (group before A23). After: co-occur 0.55, A23-only 0.45, A23 before group 0.545, group before A23 0.005. So order flipped: before group → A23; after A23 → group (when both occur).

- REL025-029 (A26 with A31/A32/A37/A38/A39): before co-occur 1.0, B_before_A 1.0 (group before A26). After: co-occur 0.55, A26-only 0.45, B_before_A 0.55 (group before A26 still). So A26 always occurs; group (when present) still before A26.

- REL030-039 (pairs within the group A31/A32/A37/A38/A39): before co-occurrence 1.0, order mixed (A_before_B ~0.5, B_before_A ~0.5) — so the group members execute in no fixed order relative to each other. After: co-occurrence 0.55, neither 0.45, and among co-occurring, order still mixed. Wait — "neither" 0.45? But A31 participation after is 0.55 and A32 0.55... If they were perfectly correlated (all five together in 55% of traces), then neither = 0.45. Yes: after, either all five group activities occur together (55% of traces) or none of them (45%). And REL015-019 show A22 vs group: mutually exclusive. So after: in ~55% of traces the group {A31,A32,A37,A38,A39} executes (in mixed order), in ~45% A22 executes instead; they almost never co-occur (0.005).

Hmm wait, but REL015: A_only 0.45 (A22 without A31), B_only 0.545 (A31 without A22), co-occurrence 0.005. And A22 participation after = 0.455, group participation 0.55. So yes: A22 and the group became alternatives.

Before: A22 participation 1.0, group participation 1.0 each, co-occurrence 1.0. So before, both always executed: A22 and all five group activities in every trace.

Now DIR:
- Before, A20 → five successors (A31/A32/A37/A38/A39) with shares ~0.17-0.24 each. After, A20 → A23 0.995.
- Before, A21 → A22 1.0. After, A21 → A22 0.455, and → group members ~0.07-0.17.

Hmm, wait. DIR shares are over observed outgoing transitions of the source activity. Before, A21 always → A22. After, A21's outgoing transitions: 45.5% to A22, rest to group members.

Let me reconstruct the before process:
- A20 (participation 1.0, position mean ~0.32) → one of {A31, A32, A37, A38, A39} (roughly uniform).
- The group members lead to each other and to A23 (DIR003-007 before: each group member's outgoing includes the other four group members and A23, shares ~0.17-0.245). This suggests the group executes in a mixed/parallel order (each member followed by other members or by A23 when it's the last).
- A23 (position ~0.48) → ... A21? Let's check: REL008 before: A31 before A21. POS: A21 mean position before 0.618, A23 0.484, A22 0.644, A26 0.671.
- A21 → A22 (DIR002 before: A22 1.0). A22 position 0.644. A22 → A26 (REL014: A22 before A26). A26 position 0.671.

So before: A20 → group (5 activities, mixed order) → A23 → A21 → A22 → A26. All mandatory, participation 1.0.

Wait, but DIR001 before: A20's outgoing goes to group members, not to A23. And group members' outgoing includes A23. So A20 → group → A23. Then A23 → A21 presumably (not directly evidenced, but REL020-024 show group before A23; POS004 A23 at 0.48; POS002 A21 at 0.62). REL008: A31 before A21 — consistent.

After:
- A20 → A23 (0.995). So A20 now leads directly to A23, bypassing the group... but wait, the group still occurs in 55% of traces. Where does the group go?

- A21 → A22 (0.455) or → group members (~0.545 total). So after, A21 leads either to A22 or into the group.
- Group members after: lead to each other, A26 (~0.14-0.25), and A23 mostly gone (except A38 0.009). So the group, when it executes after A21, ends in A26.
- REL020-024 after: A23 before group (0.545) when both occur. So the group now comes after A23.
- REL008-012 after: A21 before group (0.545). So A21 → group.
- REL025-029 after: group before A26 (0.55). So group → A26.
- REL013 after: A23 without A22 0.545, A23 before A22 0.455. So A23 → A21 → A22 → A26 in the A22-branch.
- REL014 after: A22 before A26 0.455, A26-only 0.545.

So after: A20 → A23 → A21 → then either A22 → A26 (45.5% of traces) or the group {A31,A32,A37,A38,A39} (mixed order) → A26 (55% of traces). A22 and the group became mutually exclusive alternatives between A21 and A26.

Before: A20 → group (mixed) → A23 → A21 → A22 → A26, all mandatory.

So the change: the group of five activities {A31, A32, A37, A38, A39} moved from before A23 (between A20 and A23) to after A21 (between A21 and A26), and became an alternative to A22 (executed in ~55% of traces instead of A22). Before, both the group and A22 always executed; after, exactly one of them executes per trace (group ~55 in 100, A22 ~45 in 100).

Hmm, wait. Let me double check the "before" order of A22 and the group. REL015-019 before: B_before_A = 1.0 where A = A22, B = group member. So group before A22. And REL008-012 before: B_before_A = 1.0 where A = A21, B = group member. So group before A21. And REL001 before: A20 before A22. REL007: A21 before A22. REL013 before: A23 before A22 (B_before_A where A=A22, B=A23 → A23 before A22). REL014: A22 before A26.

So before: A20 → group → A23 → ... → A21 → A22 → A26. Wait, but where does A21 sit relative to A23? REL008 before: A31 before A21. POS: A23 mean 0.484, A21 mean 0.618. So A23 before A21. So before: A20 → {group, mixed} → A23 → A21 → A22 → A26.

After: A20 → A23 (DIR001). A23 → A21 (POS004 A23 mean 0.38, POS002 A21 mean 0.526; REL020-024: A23 before group). A21 → A22 or group (DIR002). Group → A26 (REL025-029: group before A26; DIR003-007: group members → A26). A22 → A26 (REL014: A22 before A26 0.455).

So after: A20 → A23 → A21 → {A22 | group} → A26.

So the group moved from before A23 to after A21, and became an alternative to A22. This is a structural change: a block of activities was relocated and made optional/alternative.

Now, what hypothesis does this support? The evidence directly shows:
1. Participation changes: A22 dropped from always to ~45.5 in 100; group members dropped from always to ~55 in 100.
2. Mutual exclusivity: A22 and group now almost never co-occur (REL015-019).
3. Ordering: group moved from before A23/A21 to after A21/A23 (REL008-012, REL020-024 order flip; DIR001 A20 now → A23 directly; DIR002 A21 now → group).
4. POS shifts consistent: A23 moved earlier (0.484 → 0.380), A21 earlier (0.618 → 0.526), group members later (0.40 → 0.57-0.59), A22 slightly earlier (0.644 → 0.596), A20 slightly later (0.324 → 0.350), A26 slightly earlier (0.671 → 0.645).

LAG items: LAG001-010 have support after = 1 (only 1 observation!). These are pairs like (A20, A31) — before, the pair occurred within 5 steps in 200 traces; after, only 1 trace. Wait, support for LAG is "traces containing the ordered pair within five steps". After, A20 → A23 directly, so A20→A31 within 5 steps rarely happens. The after profiles are based on 1 observation each — very weak. These LAG items show the before-lag distribution (uniform over 1-5) vs after (single value). Given support after = 1, these are weak. But they're consistent with the relocation: e.g., LAG003 (A20, A37): after lag 1 in the single observation — hmm, A20 → A37 directly? DIR001 after shows A20 → A37 0.005. So in 1 trace A20 → A37 directly. These single-observation LAG items are consistent but weak. I should mention them cautiously or not lean on them.

Actually wait — the LAG items qualified as evidence, but with support after = 1, the proportions are based on 1 observation. I should treat them as weak and not build the hypothesis on them. The core hypothesis rests on OCC, DIR, POS, REL items with solid support.

TWAIT001: (A26, A19) elapsed time between consecutive completions decreased from mean ~0.94 h to ~0.45 h (56 observations each window). This is a timing change — a hypothesis in its own right. The time family had 1 item vs 0.019 expected. Per the instructions: "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces". So the single TWAIT item is within what chance produces for the time family. Hmm, but 0.019 expected means ~2% of stable processes produce one item. So 1 item is unusual but the instruction explicitly says one or two items when fewer than one is expected is what unchanged processes typically produce → treat as insufficient on its own. But the control-flow family has overwhelming evidence (72 vs 0.72).

So overall: the change is in control flow. The main hypothesis: the block {A31, A32, A37, A38, A39} was relocated from the segment between A20 and A23 to the segment between A21 and A26, where it now alternates with A22 (mutually exclusive), with the group taken in about 55 in 100 cases and A22 in about 45 in 100; previously both always executed.

Wait — is it "relocated" or is it that A20 now bypasses the group? Let me re-check. Before: A20 → group. After: A20 → A23. And A21 → group. Before: A21 → A22 only. So the group's position changed from after A20/before A23 to after A21/before A26. That's a relocation of the block, plus a change from mandatory to optional (alternative with A22).

Actually, let me reconsider: is it a swap? Before: A20 → group → A23 → A21 → A22 → A26. After: A20 → A23 → A21 → {group | A22} → A26. So the group moved from before A23 to after A21 — it swapped with the segment A23→A21→A22? Not exactly a swap; the group now competes with A22.

Hmm, actually let me reconsider whether A22 is still after A21 in the after window. DIR002 after: A21 → A22 0.455. REL007 after: A21 and A22 co-occur 0.455, A21 before A22 0.455, A21-only 0.545. So when A22 occurs, A21 before it. REL013 after: A23 before A22 0.455 (when co-occurring). So A22 still sits between A21 and A26 in the traces where it occurs.

And the group after: A21 before group (REL008-012), group before A26 (REL025-029), group members lead to A26 (DIR003-007 after: A26 share 0.14-0.25). Also group members lead to each other (mixed order maintained, REL030-039 after: among co-occurring, mixed orders).

So the after structure: A20 → A23 → A21 → (A22 → A26) or (group in mixed order → A26).

The main hypothesis: a structural relocation — the five-activity block {A31, A32, A37, A38, A39} moved from before A23 to after A21 and became an alternative to A22 (XOR choice), whereas before both the block and A22 were mandatory in sequence.

Is this "Supported hypothesis" or "Weak hypothesis"? The evidence is direct, consistent, and massive: 72 control-flow items vs 0.72 expected. The relational evidence directly shows the order flip and mutual exclusivity. Participation changes are direct. DIR shows the new edges (A20→A23, A21→group, group→A26) and loss of old ones (A20→group, A21→A22 only). POS shifts are consistent. Competing explanations: could this be a sampling artifact? No — 72 items vs 0.72 expected; empirical strength 0.995 across the board. Could the group have been "replaced" rather than "moved"? The evidence shows the group still executes in 55% of traces, in mixed order, now after A21 and before A26 — that's direct relational evidence of the new position. The old position (before A23) is directly contradicted: A20 now → A23 directly (0.995), group before A23 dropped to 0.005, A23 before group 0.545.

One competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out: the two windows are finite samples; but with 200 traces each and these effect sizes, that's not plausible. Another: maybe there are two separate changes (group made optional AND order changed) rather than one relocation — but the evidence consistently points to one structural rearrangement. Also, the LAG items are based on a single after-observation each, so they add little.

What about the "change in how often existing paths are taken" condition? That doesn't apply here — this is a relocation + optionality change, not a path-frequency shift. The instructions say: "It does not apply when an activity or path is (nearly) absent in one window..." — here nothing is absent; the group and A22 both occur substantially in both windows. But the change is not merely shares shifting: the order flipped and mutual exclusivity appeared. So the hypothesis is about order/placement, supported by REL/DIR/POS directly. Good.

Support level: Supported hypothesis. The evidence directly and consistently shows the relocation and the new alternative relationship. Limitations: LAG profiles rest on a single after-observation each; the exact internal routing shares of the group (which member follows which) can't be pinned down beyond "mixed order"; and the single time item is within chance expectation for its family, so it should be reported as an observed difference but not merged into the main hypothesis.

Wait — should TWAIT001 be part of the main hypothesis? The instructions: "A consistent change in these times is a hypothesis in its own right (a change in timing); it does not need a structural counterpart." But also the screening comparison: time family 1 item vs 0.019 expected — that's roughly what an unchanged process produces occasionally (the instruction's example: "one or two items when fewer than one is expected"). So the TWAIT item alone doesn't establish a timing change. It's one item, consistent decrease (mean, median, q25, q75, std all down), empirical strength 0.9995, 56 observations each side. Hmm. The mean dropped from ~0.94h to ~0.45h — halved. With 56 observations per window and empirical strength 0.9995 (out of 2000 reference comparisons), that's a strong single item. But the family-level expectation says 1 item is within what chance produces. The instruction is explicit: "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks." That applies to choosing the overall support level when the total count is at chance level. Here the total is dominated by control flow (72 vs 0.72), so the overall level is driven by control flow. For the TWAIT item, I should report it as an observed difference but note that a single time item is within what an unchanged process produces, so it doesn't establish a timing change.
